newsitem.title: SPAIN: EU envoy won't compete with U.S. in Mideast - Spain.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy won't compete with U.S. in Mideast - Spain.

text.p: Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Tuesday the European Union's Middle East envoy would complement Washington's efforts, not compete with them.
The 15-nation group named on Monday Spanish ambassador to Israel Miguel Angel Moratinos as its special envoy to track the Middle East peace process.

"Of course there is no attempt to establish a competition between the United States and the European Union but precisely to complement, because the U.S. has always been a great political actor in the region while the European Union has been the great economic actor," Matutes told reporters.
Europe has seized on the latest crisis in the Middle East to enhance its political influence in the region where it is the main paymaster.
Matutes said more than 50 percent of the financial aid Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza receive comes from the EU and more than 60 percent of total Israeli foreign trade is with the EU.

Europe has "vital" interests in the Middle East and if the peace process were derailed Europe would have to bear the cost -- "fundamentalist terrorism, an increase in the price of petroleum and additional aid to countries in the region," Matutes added.
